toolchain.gate: Exit 0 is NOT sufficient — Godot 4.7.1 exits 0 when the script fails to PARSE. Green means the run also printed `test_all: N checks passed` with N above the previous count and no FAIL lines.

priorState: Rows 0.1-0.9 are done and committed (72a4a91, ab5a1f9, f912540, a039e95, 110f391). Autoloads registered, in Doc 00 §2.2 order: Tokens, Weirdness, Settings, GameState, RuntimeEvents. core/ holds palette.gd, character_proportions.gd, tube.gd, eyes.gd, save_data.gd, runtime_event.gd — all with class_name. tests/test_all.gd is green at 215 checks and awaits one process_frame before running anything. tests/harness.gd currently holds only the expect()/expect_eq()/report()/exit_code() bookkeeping; its own header says the pure runtime harness — reset(), enqueue(), step() and the Player/Journal/ZoneManager/Health stubs — arrives with this row.

architecture.decision: The resolver reaches every other system through duck-typed, nullable references it holds as fields (`player`, `zone_manager`), assigned by SessionDirector at row 0.12 and by the test harness at row 0.10. It never names an autoload singleton that is not yet registered.
alternatives: Reference CombatDirector / CutsceneDirector / TransitionDirector / ZoneManager as autoload singletons, as later document snippets do. Impossible today: GDScript resolves autoload names at compile time, and none of those four is registered until rows 0.11, 0.12 and 2.3. The file would not parse.

Build only the arms whose systems already exist and add the rest per later row. Rejected: the priority ladder IS the deliverable of this row, and a ladder missing rungs cannot be tested for ordering, which is the only property that matters here.
Introduce an interface/base class per collaborator. Rejected under ponytail — one implementation each, and GDScript duck-types anyway.
seams: `RuntimeDirector.player` and `RuntimeDirector.zone_manager` are assignment points, not a plugin system. Doc 00 §12's own harness is described as stubbing Player, Journal, ZoneManager and Health, so the substitution seam is document-mandated, not invented. Nothing else gets a nullable field until a row proves it needs one.
The resolver stays a pure function of (queue, state): `_resolve()` reads RuntimeEvents and the fields above, and writes only committed state. No arm awaits, starts a tween, or reads wall-clock time.

Every duration the director owns is an integer tick count derived from the owning document's float constant (Doc 00 §2.4), never an integer literal. The overlay tween mirrors `_lock_ticks`; it never gates it (§4.5, contract 21).

`_resolve_locked()` passes RESPAWN_REQUEST and nothing else. Every other event published under a lock is discarded on purpose (§6.3) — that discard is a feature, and a future row must not 'fix' it by deferring more.

`defer()` is used for exactly the three §4.6 rows: CUTSCENE_REQUEST, CHECKPOINT_REACHED / SECRET_REVEAL_REQUEST published during a seamless activation, and CHAPTER_ADVANCE_REQUEST. Everything else is discarded and re-detected.

The minimal `PlayerController` created here owns Doc 00 §5.1's ten-value `State` enum and nothing else of substance. Row 1.4 fills in movement, the per-state arms and DEPTH_RATIO; it does not move or redefine the enum.
architecture.note: One fork, decided once: how a resolver written before its collaborators reaches them. Everything else in this row is transcription of Doc 00 §4.

tasks.title: Add the RuntimeDirector resolver and register it
tasks.intent: Create res://autoload/runtime_director.gd per Doc 00 §4 — priority 100 pinned in `_ready()` with a runtime assert, `_physics_process` running swap / poll / tick-durations / resolve, the full fifteen-rung `_resolve()` ladder of §4.2, `_resolve_locked()`, `_tick_durations()`, and the tick-counted transition lock of §4.5 — and register it in project.godot as the last autoload.
tasks.constraints: Follow Doc 00 §4.1's skeleton for structure and §4.2's table for order; every one of the fifteen rungs exists as its own `_try_*` method in the authored order, each returning true only if it committed. Honour the two stated exceptions exactly: `_try_damage()` applies and then cancels lower intents rather than ending the tick, and `_try_zone_travel()` never ends the tick on a SEAMLESS activation (§4.5). Lock rules per §4.5: GATED_ZONE_REQUEST, SEAM_FALLBACK_REQUEST and a cross-zone RESPAWN_REQUEST take the lock and set ZONE_TRANSITION; ZONE_ACTIVATION_REQUEST takes no lock and leaves the player FREE or DRIVING. §7.8: a zone request committed at priority 2 sets `_pending_blackout = true` instead of letting LETHAL_DAMAGE begin a blackout this tick. §4.6: defer exactly CUTSCENE_REQUEST, CHAPTER_ADVANCE_REQUEST, and CHECKPOINT_REACHED / SECRET_REVEAL_REQUEST published during a seamless activation — discard everything else. `_resolve_locked()` consumes only RESPAWN_REQUEST and discards the rest (§6.3, §11.1). Durations are integer tick counts derived from the owning document's float constant per §2.4 — define `const TICK := 1.0 / 60.0` and derive FADE_TICKS from §7.4's 0.35 s, DOOR_WIPE_TICKS from §7.6's 0.25 s, SEAM_WIPE_TICKS from §7.4's 0.12 s, arrival grace from §7.7's 0.15 s, and the blackout count from Doc 02 §7.3's 0.6 s; never write the integers 21, 15, 7 or 9 as literals. No `await`, no `create_tween()`, no `get_tree().create_timer()`, no `Input.*` anywhere in this file. Reach collaborators only through the nullable duck-typed fields `player` and `zone_manager`, never by naming an unregistered autoload — CombatDirector, CutsceneDirector, TransitionDirector, ZoneManager, AudioDirector and SessionDirector do not exist yet and naming any of them fails to parse. Where a rung's full commit needs one of those systems, commit the part the director owns (player state, lock ticks, pending flags, the committed signal) and leave a `ponytail:` comment naming the tracker row that completes it — do not invent a placeholder subsystem. Emit the committed-domain signals §6.2 names: checkpoint_committed, secret_revealed, damage_committed, zone_entered, chapter_advanced. Expose the lock entry points §12 check 20 exercises: gated transition, door wipe, boot, and respawn, all releasing control when `_lock_ticks` reaches 0. `_poll_contacts()` exists as an empty hook with a comment naming row 4.1 — hitboxes do not exist yet. In project.godot, append RuntimeDirector after RuntimeEvents and change nothing else; add a comment noting that Doc 00 §2.2 places it twelfth and that rows 0.11, 0.12 and 2.3 insert their autoloads ABOVE it, since it must be registered last.

All fifteen rungs present in §4.2's order with their §4.2/§5.1 preconditions; `_resolve_locked()` passes only RESPAWN_REQUEST; lock is a tick countdown released in `_tick_durations()`; four named lock entry points (gated, door, boot/`take_lock`, blackout+respawn). deviations: §4.1's skeleton shows no step 4f. Deferral lives in `_defer_survivors()`, called from `_physics_process()` after `_resolve()`, so `_resolve()` stays exactly the fifteen rungs. A harness that calls `_resolve()` alone therefore does NOT exercise §4.6 — `step()` must mirror `_physics_process()`.

§4.6 (three events always survive) versus §6.3/§11.1 (everything published behind an opaque overlay is discarded) is a genuine conflict. §6.3 wins: `_defer_survivors()` returns early while locked or in BLACKOUT. Doc 00 §4.1's own `_resolve_locked()` comment — 'Everything else published this tick is discarded by design' — is what settles it. Deferring instead would carry a cutscene request across an entire transition and fire it on arrival.

§4.5's table names only a CROSS-ZONE respawn as taking the lock, but §11.2 step 8 fades in and releases either way, so a same-zone respawn takes a FADE_TICKS lock — otherwise control returns under an opaque overlay.

§11.2 step 1 says RESPAWN_REQUEST is 'queued' and names no publisher. The director enqueues it when its own blackout countdown expires, on the same reasoning §4.1 gives for a gated transition ending being the lock's own completion. Without a publisher, §12 check 19 deadlocks.
§7.6's door wipe has no authored carrier. The GATED_ZONE_REQUEST payload key `wipe_ticks` defaults to FADE_TICKS; row 2.5's DoorBoundary sets DOOR_WIPE_TICKS.
TransitionTeardown is read as a payload Dictionary, not the §7.4.1 Resource — tracker Deferred D1, as authored.
tasks.finding: `tests/test_all.gd`'s standing comment that 'a --script SceneTree does not instantiate project autoloads' is wrong on Godot 4.7.1. Verified directly: after one `await process_frame`, root's children are Tokens, Weirdness, Settings, GameState, RuntimeEvents and RuntimeDirector, with `_ready()` already run. What a --script run lacks is the GDScript GLOBAL IDENTIFIER at the script's own compile time, because the script compiles before autoloads instantiate. The distinction matters from this row on: RuntimeDirector reads the RuntimeEvents SINGLETON, so a check that instantiates its own copy of runtime_events.gd is talking to a queue the director never reads. Use `root.get_node(^"RuntimeDirector")` and the live queue.

tasks.title: Build the pure runtime harness and write checks 15, 4, 17 and 20
tasks.intent: Complete res://tests/harness.gd with Doc 00 §12's pure runtime harness — reset(), enqueue(), step() and the Player / Journal / ZoneManager / Health / interactable stubs — and append tracker row 0.10's Verify column to res://tests/test_all.gd: Doc 00 §12 checks 15, 4, 17 and 20.
tasks.constraints: Keep harness.gd's two jobs separate exactly as its header already states: the expect()/expect_eq()/report()/exit_code() bookkeeping is untouched, and the runtime harness is added beside it. Do not add a class_name — the header explains why, and the reason has not changed. A `--script` SceneTree does not instantiate project autoloads, so the harness instantiates runtime_events.gd and runtime_director.gd itself and adds them to root, the pattern rows 0.6 and 0.9 already use; assert the project registration separately. The stubs are the smallest objects that answer what the resolver asks: a PlayerController instance whose `state` the test sets directly, a Journal stub with `blocks_zone_travel()` and a settable state, a ZoneManager stub with `current` and a counting `activate_zone()`, a Health stub with `current` / `max_pips` and a counting `take_damage()`, and an interactable stub counting `interact()` calls. `step()` drives one resolve without a physics server — swap, tick durations, resolve — and must never await a frame. Free every instantiated node at the end of the check so the suite leaks nothing. The four checks to write, all four of which must genuinely bite: (15) RuntimeDirector.process_physics_priority is 100 after _ready(), which is above every gameplay node's default 0 and above CombatDirector's 50, and ZoneManager's 110 is deliberately higher because it streams after the commit — assert the number and its relation, not just the number. (4) Damage and INTERACT_REQUEST in the same tick: health drops by exactly one and interact() is never called. (17) A seamless ZONE_ACTIVATION_REQUEST leaves _lock_ticks at 0 and the player FREE, and a DAMAGE event published in the same tick still lands — a seam is not a shield; a GATED_ZONE_REQUEST in the same situation takes the lock, sets ZONE_TRANSITION, and ends the tick so a same-tick interact does not commit. (20) With no tween in existence at all, a gated transition, a door wipe, a boot lock and a respawn each release control exactly when _lock_ticks reaches 0 — step the resolver its declared number of ticks, assert control is still locked at one tick before, and FREE at zero. Do not weaken, reword or renumber any existing check. Add each new check under a comment naming the tracker row and the Doc 00 §12 number, matching the file's existing style.
tasks.acceptance: `godot --headless --script res://tests/test_all.gd` prints `test_all: N checks passed` with N above 215 and no FAIL lines. Each of the four checks is proven to bite by temporarily breaking the thing it guards — dropping process_physics_priority to 0, letting _try_interact() run after damage, giving the seamless path a lock, and releasing control on a frame count rather than _lock_ticks — and each of those four edits must fail the suite. Report the observed failure counts; revert every temporary edit before finishing.
